raw_text:
Below is a complete 12-week hypertrophy program for your client, organized into three progressive phases, with week-by-week structure, session details (exercises, sets, reps, tempos, rest), plus a vegan nutrition plan to reach 150 g protein/day and guidance on recovery.

Overview
- Frequency: 4 lifting days/week (Upper/Lower split) + 1 optional accessory/conditioning day
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–4: Foundation Hypertrophy (technique, volume base)
  - Weeks 5–8: Progressive Overload (intensity and volume progression)
  - Weeks 9–12: Intensification and Specialization (heavier loads, advanced techniques, targeted weak points)
- Progression: Double progression within rep ranges; add 2.5–5 lb (1–2.5 kg) when top of rep range is met for all sets with good form.
- Tempo: Unless stated, use 3-1-1-0 (eccentric-pause-concentric-pause) for compounds, 2-1-2-0 for isolation.
- Rest: 90–120s for big compounds; 60–90s for accessories; 30–45s for small isolations or supersets.
- RPE: Aim RPE 7–9 on final set for main lifts.

Phase 1: Foundation Hypertrophy (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: Groove technique, build volume tolerance, establish mind–muscle connection, set baselines.

Week 1
- Upper A
  - Barbell bench press: 4×8, RPE 7
  - One-arm DB row: 4×10/side
  - Seated DB shoulder press: 3×10
  - Lat pulldown (medium grip): 3×10–12
  - Cable fly: 3×12–15
  - DB lateral raise: 3×12–15
  - EZ-bar curl: 3×10–12
  - Cable rope triceps pressdown: 3×10–12
- Lower A
  - Back squat: 4×8, RPE 7
  - Romanian deadlift: 4×8
  - Walking lunges: 3×10/leg
  - Leg press: 3×12
  - Seated leg curl: 3×12–15
  - Standing calf raise: 4×12–15
  - Ab wheel or cable crunch: 3×12–15
- Upper B
  - Incline DB press: 4×8–10
  - Chest-supported T-bar row: 4×8–10
  - Arnold press: 3×10
  - Wide-grip pull-up or assisted pull-up: 4×6–8
  - Cable face pull: 3×12–15
  - DB incline curl: 3×10–12
  - Overhead cable triceps extension: 3×10–12
- Lower B
  - Deadlift (conventional or sumo): 4×5–6, RPE 7
  - Front squat or goblet squat: 3×8–10
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3×8/leg
  - Hip thrust: 4×8–10
  - Leg extension: 3×12–15
  - Seated calf raise: 4×12–15
  - Side plank: 3×30–45s/side

Week 2
- Repeat Week 1 structure; add 2.5–5 lb where possible or +1 rep per set within ranges. Keep RPE ≤8.

Week 3
- Same splits; push upper compounds to 4×6–8 where noted:
  - Bench: 4×6–8 (slightly heavier)
  - Row variations: 4×8–10
  - Squat: 4×6–8 (slightly heavier)
  - Deadlift: 4×4–5, RPE 8
  - Accessories maintain 10–15 reps; try to add load or reps.

Week 4 (Deload-lite)
- Reduce volume by ~30–40% and keep intensity ~60–70% of Week 3 loads.
- Use perfect tempo and stop sets at RPE 6–7.
- Keep movement patterns but do 2 sets/exercise, cap reps at mid-range.

Phase 2: Progressive Overload (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Increase intensity and total weekly volume modestly; emphasize posterior chain and upper back to support heavy pressing and squatting.

Week 5
- Upper A (Horizontal focus)
  - Barbell bench press: 5×5–6, RPE 8
  - Chest-supported row: 4×8
  - Weighted push-up or machine press: 3×8–10
  - One-arm lat pulldown: 3×10/side
  - Cable fly (low-to-high): 3×12–15
  - Lateral raise mechanical drop set: 3 rounds (10 partials + 10 full ROM)
  - Barbell curl: 3×8–10; Incline DB curl: 2×12 (superset)
  - Rope pressdown: 3×10–12; DB kickback: 2×12–15 (superset)
- Lower A (Knee-dominant)
  - Back squat: 5×5–6, RPE 8
  - Hack squat or leg press: 4×8–10
  - Walking lunges: 3×12/leg
  - Leg extension: 3×12–15 (2s squeeze)
  - Standing calf raise: 5×10–12
  - Cable crunch: 4×12–15
- Upper B (Vertical focus)
  - Overhead press (barbell or DB): 4×6–8
  - Weighted pull-up or heavy lat pulldown: 5×5–6
  - Incline DB press: 4×8–10
  - Single-arm cable row: 3×10–12/side (2s squeeze)
  - Rear-delt fly (reverse pec deck): 4×12–15
  - Preacher curl: 3×10–12
  - Overhead rope extension: 3×10–12
- Lower B (Hip-dominant)
  - Deadlift: 5×3–5, RPE 8
  - Hip thrust: 4×6–8 (2s hold at top)
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3×8–10/leg
  - Seated leg curl: 4×10–12
  - Glute med cable abduction: 3×12–15/side
  - Seated calf raise: 4×12–15
  - Pallof press: 3×12/side

Week 6
- Aim to add 2.5–5 lb to compounds or +1 rep/set if within range. Keep last set RPE 8–9.
- Optional Day 5 (Accessory/Conditioning, 20–30 min):
  - Sled push or bike intervals: 8×20s hard/100s easy
  - Arm/shoulder pump: 2–3 exercises, 2–3 sets each, 12–20 reps, low fatigue.

Week 7
- Slight variation to reduce monotony:
  - Swap bench → close-grip bench (still horizontal focus) 4×6–8
  - Swap chest-supported row → Pendlay row 4×6–8
  - Swap back squat → safety bar squat 4×6–8
  - Deadlift → RDL 4×6–8; Hip thrust stays
  - Keep rep targets similar; push accessories to the top of ranges.

Week 8 (Deload-lite)
- Reduce sets by ~40%; keep two top sets on main lifts at RPE 7.
- Prioritize technique, pauses, tempo control.

Phase 3: Intensification and Specialization (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Heavier loads in moderate rep ranges, introduce advanced hypertrophy methods, and add specialization for lagging areas (choose chest/shoulders or glutes/hamstrings based on progress; below assumes glutes/hamstrings specialization).

Week 9
- Upper A
  - Bench press: 4×4–6 (heavy), then back-off set 1×8–10 at ~85% of top weight
  - One-arm DB row: 4×8–10
  - Incline DB press: 3×8–10 (rest–pause on last set: 10 + 4–5 + 3)
  - Wide-grip pull-up: 4×6–8
  - Cable fly: 3×12–15
  - Lateral raise: 4×12–15 (last set drop set)
  - Superset: EZ curl 3×8–10 + Rope pressdown 3×10–12
- Lower A (Glute/Ham focus)
  - Deadlift: 5×3–4, RPE 8–9
  - Hip thrust: 4×6–8 with 2–3s peak contraction
  - 45° back extension (glute bias): 3×12–15 holding DB
  - Nordic curl or assisted: 3×4–6 (controlled eccentrics)
  - Leg curl: 3×10–12
  - Standing calf raise: 4×10–12
- Upper B
  - Overhead press: 4×5–7
  - Meadows row or chest-supported row: 4×8–10
  - Close-grip bench or dip (assisted/weighted): 3×6–8
  - Lat pulldown (neutral grip): 3×8–10 (2s squeeze)
  - Rear-delt cable fly: 3×15–20
  - Hammer curl: 3×10–12
  - Cable overhead triceps: 3×10–12
- Lower B (Glute/Ham focus)
  - Front squat: 4×5–7
  - Romanian deadlift: 4×6–8
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3×8–10/leg
  - Hip abduction machine: 3×12–15
  - Seated calf raise: 4×12–15
  - Hanging leg raise: 3×10–12

Week 10
- Progress Week 9 loads/reps. Add one intensifier on an accessory in each session (drop set or rest–pause) but keep compounds strict (no grinders; RPE ≤9).

Week 11
- Chest/Shoulder secondary specialization (to balance volume)
  - Upper A: Pause bench (2s at chest) 4×4–6; Incline cable press 3×8–10; Row variations unchanged; add extra lateral raise set (total 5 sets)
  - Lower A: Maintain Week 9
  - Upper B: Add machine chest press 2×12–15 at end; keep OHP; pull volume steady
  - Lower B: Maintain Week 9, push RDL and front squat if recovering well
- Keep weekly total hard sets per muscle group around:
  - Quads: 12–14; Glutes/Hams: 14–16; Chest: 12–14; Back: 14–16; Delts: 10–12; Arms: 8–10

Week 12 (Peak + Taper)
- First half of week: Hit top sets
  - Bench: work to top set 1×3–4 @ RPE 9, back-off 2×5 @ -10%
  - Squat: 1×3–4 @ RPE 9, back-off 2×5
  - Deadlift: 1×2–3 @ RPE 9, back-off 2×4
  - OHP: 1×3–4 @ RPE 9, back-off 2×5
  - Accessories: reduce to 2 sets each, pump-focused 10–15 reps
- End of week: Reduce volume 50%, keep movement quality high. Prepare for next mesocycle with notes on best lifts, weak points, and favorite accessories.

Weekly Structure and Session Flow
- Example schedule: Mon Upper A, Tue Lower A, Thu Upper B, Fri Lower B, Sat optional accessory/conditioning; Wed/Sun rest.
- Warm-up (10–12 min): 5 min cyc/bike/row; dynamic drills (band pull-aparts, shoulder CARs, leg swings, hip openers); 2–4 ramp-up sets for first compound.
- Cool-down (5–8 min): Easy cardio + breathing, light mobility on tight areas.

Load Progression Rules
- Within a given rep range, add reps each week until at the top end for all sets with good form; then increase load by the smallest increment.
- If you stall 2 consecutive weeks, reduce load 5–7% and build back up (resensitization).

Vegan Nutrition Plan (150 g protein/day, muscle gain)
Caloric target
- Start: bodyweight × 16–18 kcal/day as a lean bulk estimate. For many 26-year-old active females, this may be ~2,200–2,600 kcal/day. Begin +250–300 kcal over current maintenance; adjust weekly by scale trends (+0.25–0.5% bodyweight/week).
- Macros: 
  - Protein: 150 g (600 kcal)
  - Fat: 70–85 g (630–765 kcal; ~0.8–1.0 g/kg)
  - Carbs: remainder (approx. 250–350 g depending on kcal)

Protein distribution
- Aim 4–5 feedings/day with 25–40 g protein each to maximize MPS.
- Leucine: Ensure 2–3 g leucine per meal. Use soy, pea–rice blends, or add 2–3 g free leucine to lower-leucine meals if needed.

Sample full day (approx. 2,400–2,500 kcal; 155–165 g protein)
- Breakfast: Tofu scramble (200 g firm tofu) with veggies, nutritional yeast; 2 slices whole-grain toast; avocado
  - ~40 g protein
- Snack: Protein shake (30 g pea–rice blend) + banana + 1 tbsp peanut butter
  - ~27–30 g protein
- Lunch: Lentil–quinoa bowl: 1 cup cooked lentils, 1 cup cooked quinoa, roasted veg, tahini–lemon sauce
  - ~35 g protein
- Pre-workout: Soy yogurt (200 g) with berries and maple syrup; small handful almonds
  - ~16–20 g protein
- Post-workout/Dinner: Tempeh stir-fry (150–200 g tempeh) over brown rice with edamame
  - ~40–45 g protein
- Optional pre-bed: Soy milk (300 ml) cocoa + 15 g pumpkin seeds
  - ~12–15 g protein

High-protein vegan staples and targets
- Soy foods: tofu, tempeh, edamame, soy milk, soy yogurt (high leucine, complete protein)
- Protein powders: pea–rice blend or soy isolate; target 1–2 scoops/day to help consistency
- Legumes: lentils, chickpeas, black beans; combine with grains (quinoa, brown rice) for complete amino profile
- Seitan: high protein wheat gluten (if gluten-tolerant)
- Nuts/seeds: pumpkin, hemp, chia; good for fats and added protein
- Fortified foods: B12, calcium, vitamin D, iodine

Peri-workout nutrition
- 60–90 min pre: 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein (e.g., soy yogurt + fruit; toast + tofu)
- Post: 30–60 g carbs + 25–40 g protein (shake or meal). Add 3–5 g creatine monohydrate daily (vegan-friendly).

Supplements (vegan-friendly)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day
- Protein powder: to hit 150 g/day
- Vitamin B12: 1,000 mcg cyanocobalamin 2–3×/week or 50–100 mcg daily
- Vitamin D3 (vegan lichen): 1,000–2,000 IU/day (adjust by bloodwork)
- Algae-based DHA/EPA: 250–500 mg/day
- Iodine: 150 mcg/day (or iodized salt)
- Iron: monitor ferritin; supplement if low (with vitamin C source)
- Calcium: aim 1,000 mg/day from diet/fortified foods; supplement to fill gaps
- Zinc: 8–12 mg/day if intake is low

Hydration and sodium
- 30–40 ml/kg/day fluids; add electrolytes around longer/hot sessions.
- Don’t overly restrict sodium during a bulk; season to taste, monitor blood pressure.

Recovery and Lifestyle
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night; consistent schedule.
- Steps: 6–10k/day to manage appetite and recovery.
- Mobility: 10 min on rest days for hips/shoulders/thoracic spine.
- Stress: 5–10 min daily down-regulation (box breathing, walks).

Progress tracking
- Bodyweight: 3–4×/week morning average; aim +0.25–0.5%/week.
- Gym: Log loads/reps/RPE. Aim to beat last week by a small margin.
- Photos/measurements every 4 weeks.
- If protein adherence dips, prioritize 1–2 shakes/day and anchor meals (breakfast and post-workout) at 30–40 g protein.

Adjustments for the trainer
- If upper body lags: shift specialization in Phase 3 to chest/shoulders (add 4–6 hard sets/wk there; pull 4–6 sets from legs).
- If fatigue high: pull one accessory per session or reduce RPE to 7–8 for a week.
- If recovery is great: add the optional Day 5 consistently with low-impact cardio and arm/delt pumps.

This plan provides a clear week-by-week framework, scalable loads, and a vegan nutrition strategy to reliably hit 150 g protein/day while supporting hypertrophy.
